source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of the exact original XML verse substring, including written/read notes, not a normalized substitute.
source.public_versification_note: Public 13–15, 16:1–35 and 18 align directly. Public 16:36–50 maps to Hebrew 17:1–15; public 17:1–13 maps to Hebrew 17:16–28. All 214 original records, including every annotation, are hashed exactly. Later numbering differences require separate mapping.

key_decisions.decision: Preserves lethal violence and the gender-specific wives and vulnerable little ones, retaining plunder’s dehumanizing image.
Preserves bread and shade metaphors, supported by a selective note, and both fear prohibitions.
Keeps both plague and disinheritance and the comparison with the proposed nation from Moses.
Keeps unusual eye-to-eye idiom rather than harmonizing mouth-to-mouth in chapter 12; retains each reported manifestation.
Preserves the harsh slaughter verb and marks the statement as the imagined nations’ explanation.

Preserves the clauses actually quoted from Exodus 34 with recognizable shared wording and poetic lineation. Retains intergenerational guilt without reducing it to natural consequences or importing omitted clauses.
Reads the glory clause within the oath; note retains possible future will-be-filled construal.
Preserves valley, tomorrow and retreat direction; Sea of Reeds follows Hebrew yam suf with conventional name noted.
Retains corpses, census scope and twenty-year threshold without extending the category to uncounted people.
Preserves raised-hand oath and both named exceptions; does not replace the oath image with abstraction.
Retains shepherd life and prostitution metaphor for faithlessness; note distinguishes figurative accusation from an asserted sexual act.
Preserves doubled day/year correspondence and forty figures; difficult tenuah rendered opposition with alternatives noted.
Follows read-form causative complaining while exact source binding includes both written/read forms.
Renders reckless presumption, retaining the contrast with Moses and ark remaining; does not invent their motives.
